newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors free bankers over Hanbo scandal.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors free bankers over Hanbo scandal.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Friday released three current or former bank chiefs who were questioned in connection with a leading steelmaker's loan scandal, the state television reported.

The Korean Broadcasting System television report quoted prosecution officials as saying that the three were found not involved in the Hanbo Steel Co loan scandal and were allowed to return home late on Friday after two days of questioning.
State prosecutors have been investigating the financial failure of Hanbo Steel, which piled up some five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions.
The steel firm, flagship unit of the nation's 14th largest conglomerate Hanbo Group, was declared insolvent on January 23.
Prosecution officials could not immediately be reached for comment.

The three bank chiefs who were questioned are Korea Exchange Bank president Chang Myung-son, state-run Korea Development Bank president Kim Shi-hyung and Cho Hung Bank's former president Lee Chong-yeon.
The banks are among the main creditors to Hanbo.
Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo and two commercial bank heads -- Sheen Kwang-shik of Korea First Bank and Woo Chan-mok of Cho Hung -- have been arrested on charges of bribery.
Chung has admitted to giving about one million dollars worth of bribes to Sheen and Woo in return for a huge amount of loans to finance construction of a new steel mill.
The arrests brought to 18 the total number of bankers who have been jailed or forced to resign since Kim swept to power in 1993 on an anti-graft platform.
Most were found to have accepted bribes from borrowers.
